audits.claim_path: certificate.py main (203-245) runs derive() (45-52), which is exact Fraction arithmetic (exact.py, pseries.py; no float enters: every S/Poly/Num coefficient is a Fraction, for example pseries.py 22, 106; exact.py 283, 299, 301, 373). It then runs the gating checks: checks() 86-103, ratio_check() 189-200 and stability() 106-114. Any failure returns 1 at 224-225, and that happens before document() at 231. document() (164-186) computes the published values: c and c2 come from num_iv (134-146), c2/c from div(c2, c) (168), and every value is published through pub() (156-158) and _round_out (149-153). num_iv works as follows. atom = mul(gam.gamma(g), gam.rpow((12,12), e)) (136). gam.gamma is exp_iv(lngamma) (gam.py 38-39), and lngamma is Stirling at q+10 (gam.py 20-35). rpow is exp_iv(from_frac(expo) * log_iv(base)) (gam.py 42-44). exp_iv/exp_pt come from elem.py 26-36, then ia.exp_neg/_exp_neg_point/_poly_exp_neg (ia.py 163-201). log_iv/log_pt come from elem.py 56-71, then _atanh_series (elem.py 40-53). The terms are from_frac(v) * PI^(h//2) * isqrt(PI)^[h odd] * isqrt(m) (certificate.py 139-144), summed outward (145). The only constants used are ia.PI (123-137), ia.LN2 (150-160) and gam.BERN (gam.py 10-11). controls.py is not imported. The atan, sin/cos, sinh/cosh, E1, L, A, Sinc and log1p code in elem.py 74-308 and Phi, Q and the Mills ratio in ia.py 204-279 are not reached.
audits.basic_operations: ia.py: dn/up are math.nextafter toward -inf/+inf (14-19). add (36-37) and sub (40-41) use the correct cross endpoints. mul (48-50) takes all four corner products and then dn(min) and up(max). This is sound because pred(fl(p)) <= p for round-to-nearest, and dn is monotone. div (53-57) raises ZeroDivisionError when 0 is in b (54-55) and otherwise uses the four quotients with outward rounding. scal (60-64) and divc (67-69) handle sign. sqr (72-78) handles all three sign cases. isqrt (110-115) raises on a negative lower end (111-112) and otherwise applies dn/up to the correctly rounded math.sqrt. certificate.py: the sums at 145 are dn/up of single additions. ipow (127-131) is repeated outward mul, with a final div for negative n (PI > 0, so no zero). The 141 - sqrt6 interval at 194 uses the correct crossed endpoints. All int-to-float conversions on the path are small and exact: float(n) at ia.py 183, float(e) at elem.py 67, float(2k+1) at elem.py 51, Fr(m) for squarefree m in {2,3,6}, and 141. math.frexp (elem.py 60) and math.ldexp (ia.py 191) are exact. With y <= 700 the ldexp result stays normal: n <= 1009 and exp(-r) >= 0.47. No fused, chained or library operation produces an enclosure. math.fsum, math.gamma, math.pi and float ** appear only in the check-only functions d1_float/num_float (certificate.py 74-83, 121-124). Float ** also appears in one remainder bound (elem.py 52; see elementary_functions). The float n = int(y/0.6931471805599453) at ia.py 182 only selects the reduction; the range check at 185-186 then verifies it. Python specifics: CPython float is IEEE binary64 round-to-nearest, with SSE2 on x86-64 hardware. CPython evaluates each bytecode operation separately, so nothing is contracted into an FMA. No numpy is used. decimal is used only in _round_out, which converts an exact Decimal(float) with an explicit ROUND_FLOOR/ROUND_CEILING under the default prec-28 context (certificate.py 150-153). Nothing on the certificate path changes the context; controls.py's getcontext is not imported. math.nextafter needs Python 3.9 or later.
audits.elementary_functions: exp(-z), Horner, ia.py 163-172: degree 18, |z| <= 0.75 enforced by the range check at 185-186. The truncation term is |z|^19/19! e^|z|; 0.75^19/19! is about 3.5e-20, under 1e-19. Each coefficient _INVFACT[i] = fl(_INVFACT[i-1]/i) (144-146) has relative error <= gamma_18. The Horner error is <= gamma_36 sum|c_i||z|^i (Higham), so the total is 54u e^|z| (1+O(u)). The code uses 56u(1+1e-12)+1e-19 times ez = 2.12 >= e^0.75 = 2.1170, so the stated derivation checks out. err (171) is computed in round-to-nearest from exact constants. That is at most about 3 roundings, roughly 3u relative, which the 2u-of-54u slack absorbs easily. Endpoints: lo = dn(p(r1) - err) and hi = up(p(r0) + err) are used correctly for the decreasing function (187-190). The range reduction y = n ln2 + r uses the rational LN2 enclosure and is verified (183-186). Scaling by 2^-n is exact. exp_neg/exp_pt/exp_iv (ia.py 194-201, elem.py 26-36) use the right monotonicity, and for t > 0 they take 1/exp(-t) through div. log, elem.py 56-71: t = m 2^e with m in [0.7071, 1.4142), so |u| = |(m-1)/(m+1)| <= 0.1716 (interval div at 65), and log t = 2 atanh u + e*LN2. _atanh_series (40-53) uses interval terms for K=26 and the tail bound m^(2K+3)/((2K+3)(1-m^2)), which is correct: it is a geometric bound on sum_{k>K} m^(2k+1)/(2k+1). The tail is computed in undirected binary64 with float pow m**55 and a safety factor of 2 (52). For reachable inputs (12, 2pi, 61/6, 65/6 and the Stirling products, all with |u| <= 0.1716) the true tail is <= about 3e-44, roughly 27 orders below the one-ulp widening of s (about 1e-17). It is sound even if pow were off by orders of magnitude, and the underflow cases are covered by the minimum-subnormal widening of _with_err (20-22). lnGamma, gam.py 20-35: Stirling at y = q+10 with K = 10. The Bernoulli numbers B2..B22 (10-11) are correct. corr and rem are exact Fractions (29-30), and rem = |B22|/(22*21*y^21), about 1e-20, is the first omitted term. For real y > 0 the classical theorem (DLMF 5.11) bounds the remainder by that term with the same sign. It is enclosed as from_frac(corr-rem)[0], from_frac(corr+rem)[1] (31). lnGamma(q) = lnGamma(q+N) - log prod_{j<N}(q+j), with the product exact (32-35). gamma is exp_iv(lngamma) and rpow is exp_iv(from_frac(expo) * log_iv(base)) (38-44). NOTE.md 167-170 matches the code.
audits.constants_and_conversions: pi: Machin 16 atan(1/5) - 4 atan(1/239) with 40 terms each. The alternating-series remainder is bounded by the first omitted term in exact Fractions, giving the two-sided rational [lo-err, lo+err] (ia.py 123-133). It is rounded outward through from_frac endpoints (136-137). ln 2: sum_{j<=80} 1/(j 2^j) as an exact lower bound, plus the tail bound 2/(J 2^J), which is valid since the tail is <= 1/((J+1)2^J). It is rounded outward (ia.py 150-160). from_frac (ia.py 27-33) compares Fr(float(q)) with q exactly and widens one ulp toward q. This relies on float(q), CPython's int/int true division for Fraction, being within one ulp of q; CPython rounds it correctly. Gamma(1/6) and Gamma(5/6) are computed, not entered. 12, 2.0, 0.5, 141 and the squarefree radicands are exact floats. The exponents -1/6, -5/6 and 2/3 enter through from_frac (gam.py 44). All exact coefficients v of the Num closed forms enter through from_frac (certificate.py 139). The publication margin MARGIN*abs(iv) (certificate.py 157) is undirected but carries no weight in the proof. Because round-to-nearest is monotone, fl(iv0 - x) <= iv0 for x >= 0 and fl(iv1 + x) >= iv1. dn/up follow (158), then decimal ROUND_FLOOR/CEILING (153). So the margin only widens. No single-float constant enters the enclosure path. The math.pi and literal floats in d1_float/num_float are check-only.
audits.decisions: No published enclosure depends on a sign or positivity decision. The values are published as sound enclosures (certificate.py 168). The gating decisions in main (213-225) can only reject, and nothing passes on failure. The exact decisions are: the theta exponent is absent (90); c equals side24 c_ref exactly for d=2,3 (93); c equals #214 C_0 and c2 equals 2B_2 exactly against d1_closed (96-99); the series are stable at orders 12/8 (114); the quadrant recurrence is consistent (exact.py 322-324); derivation ArithmeticError/ValueError returns 1 (215-217); and --check requires exact JSON equality (241). The non-exact decisions are both reject-only. (a) The d1_float/num_float tolerance test |diff| < 1e-14 (100-102) uses unenclosed math.gamma, **, math.pi and math.fsum. (b) ratio_check (198) uses the correct endpoints for a disjointness test (a[1] < q[0] or q[1] < a[0]). Overlap is only a necessary condition, so neither can certify the identity it touches (see findings). Neither affects any published enclosure. The theta exponent that num_iv drops (138) is protected by check 90, which gates document().

findings.issue: The published 'exact' c2/c closed forms (RATIO_TEXT: 54, 78, 18(141 - sqrt6)/25) are hard-coded strings. The code checks them only by an overlap test of binary64 interval enclosures (198). A non-disjoint result is necessary but not sufficient, so it does not certify the identity. The identity does hold exactly. kappa_d = c2_num/c_num gives 9/(1/6) = 54 and (26/3)/(1/9) = 78. For d=3, (165/4 - 35/4 sqrt6)/(29/72 - sqrt6/12) = 90(33 - 7 sqrt6)/(29 - 6 sqrt6) = 90(705 - 5 sqrt6)/625 = 18(141 - sqrt6)/25. An exact Num check c2_num == kappa_d * c_num would close this. The published c2/c enclosure itself, div(c2, c) at 168, is sound.

d1_float/num_float evaluate Math-#214's formulas and the closed forms with unenclosed math.gamma, float **, math.pi and math.fsum, and compare them with an absolute tolerance of 1e-14. The check is reject-only and not on the enclosure path. It is, however, the only code that ties the transcribed #214 formulas to d1_closed. The exact check (96-99) compares the derivation with d1_closed, not with #214's expression. NOTE.md section 0 and section 4.3 say the #214 identities are 'checked by the certificate'. Strictly, the bridge rests on the hand reduction in the docstring at 64-70, which I re-derived and found correct: 72^(-1/6) 6^(2/3) = 2^(1/6) 3^(1/3) = sqrt6 12^(-1/6); 3^(1/3) 6^(1/3) = 2^(1/3) 3^(2/3) = 12 sqrt3 12^(-5/6); Q = 1620 and 1620/2160 = 3/4; the results are (1/6) pi^(-3/2) and 9 pi^(-3/2). The float comparison should be described as a smoke test, not a certification.

The atanh remainder is computed in undirected binary64 with libm pow (m**55) and a safety factor of 2. This contradicts the ia.py 1-5 docstring claim that no libm transcendental is trusted. It is still sound for every reachable input. log_pt's reduction (60-65) gives |u| <= 0.1716, so the true tail is <= about 3e-44, far below the one-ulp widening of s (about 1e-17), and the underflow cases are absorbed by the minimum-subnormal step of nextafter in _with_err (20-22). An exact Fraction bound would remove the dependence on pow.

The exp Horner error bound is a hand-derived a priori bound, and err is evaluated in round-to-nearest. I checked it: coefficient error gamma_18 plus Horner error gamma_36 sum|c_i||z|^i gives 54u e^|z| (1+O(u)). The code's 56u(1+1e-12) + 1e-19 times 2.12 >= e^0.75 covers that, and the roughly 3u relative rounding in computing err is absorbed by the 2u slack. The truncation term is 0.75^19/19! e^|z|, about 3.5e-20 e^|z|. Sound, but resting on that hand analysis rather than on directed evaluation.

from_frac assumes float(q) is within one ulp of q, and it does not check that q <= up(f) or dn(f) <= q. This holds because CPython's int/int true division, used by Fraction to float, is correctly rounded. A check such as Fr(up(f)) >= q would make the routine verify itself.

The publication margin MARGIN*abs(iv) is computed undirected. It is not load-bearing: rounding is monotone, so fl(iv0 - x) <= iv0 and fl(iv1 + x) >= iv1 for x >= 0, and outward dn/up plus ROUND_FLOOR/ROUND_CEILING follow (153). The margin only adds width.

The basic-operation soundness relies on platform facts that cannot be checked by reading the code: IEEE binary64 round-to-nearest with no x87 double rounding (true on standard x86-64/SSE2 or ARM64 CPython), a correctly rounded C sqrt, and Python 3.9 or later for math.nextafter.

audits.summary: The path that produces the published enclosures is sound interval reasoning. All +, -, *, / and sqrt operations are single round-to-nearest binary64 operations, each widened outward by one ulp with nextafter: ia.py 36-57, 72-78, 110-115 and certificate.py 145. Division by an interval containing 0 raises an error (ia.py 54-55), and so does sqrt of an interval with a negative lower end (ia.py 111-112). pi, ln 2 and the Bernoulli numbers are exact rational enclosures rounded outward. exp, log, lnGamma, Gamma and 12^q have correct, verified truncation and rounding bounds and valid range reductions: ia.py 163-201, elem.py 26-71, gam.py 20-44. The undirected pieces the target note flags are all non-load-bearing or have large slack: the atanh tail (elem.py 52, true tail about 3e-44 against about 1e-17 of widening), the Horner error constant (ia.py 171, 56u against a needed 54u) and the publication margin (certificate.py 157, monotone rounding means it can only widen). All gating decisions are exact or reject-only, and none passes on failure. Two MINOR caveats concern identity claims, not bounds. First, the hard-coded exact c2/c closed forms are checked only by interval overlap (certificate.py 198). Second, the bridge between Math-#214's formulas and d1_closed is checked only by a float test with a 1e-14 tolerance (certificate.py 100-102). I verified both identities by exact hand algebra. Neither affects any published enclosure. The verdict assumes standard CPython binary64 platform behavior. It advises the A3 field only and certifies nothing.

audits.basic_operations:
Each basic operation is one correctly rounded binary64 operation on float endpoints, followed by one ulp of outward widening.
- ia.py 14-19: dn/up via math.nextafter.
- ia.py 36-41 add/sub: lower end rounded down, upper end rounded up.
- ia.py 48-50 mul: four corner products, then dn(min)/up(max).
- ia.py 53-57 div: four corner quotients; a divisor interval containing 0 raises ZeroDivisionError (54-55). main only catches RuntimeError (711-715), so this aborts the run rather than passing.
- ia.py 60-69 scal/divc: exact float scalars. The sign of c is handled; divc is only ever called with c>0.
- ia.py 72-78 sqr: sign cases handled and clamped at 0.
- ia.py 81-99 pw: odd powers by repeated outward point products; even powers through sqr.
- ia.py 110-115 isqrt: a negative lower end raises (111-112). The result is math.sqrt (correctly rounded under IEEE) then dn/up, clamped at 0.

Partial sums and products elsewhere also round outward:
- certificate.py 86, 103, 139, 157, 306-309.
- boxes.py 297-300, 311-312, 355-359, 664, 686.
- torus.py 57-61, 213.
- Products with two roundings carry an extra exact factor to cover the second rounding: boxes.py 357 (1+2^-51), certificate.py 255 (1+4e-16).

No math.fsum, math.prod, pow, ** or libm transcendental appears on the claim path:
- `**` occurs only in exact Fraction/int arithmetic (ia 128-156, torus 32/74/79, certificate 165), in the exact constant 2.0**-53, or in seeds and expansion points.
- Seeds: _guess_big/_guess_mid (boxes 97-114), _newton_big hi bracket (119), _cbrt_lo/_cbrt_iv (198, 590), _expansion_point (365).
- Expansion points are only chosen, then clamped into the rectangle, so their values carry no claim. math.sqrt(kc) at boxes 730 is the same kind of choice.
- Seeds are later verified: roots by the _sgn_f brackets (boxes 151, 188); cube roots by outward pw loops (199-200, 592-595).

Int-to-float conversions are all of small exact integers:
- float(n) with n <= 1009 (ia 183); float(j) with j <= 4001 (ia 251); float(n-1); _dfact up to 10395 (torus 194-197); cov_ref ints (torus 83); 2n+1 (ia 228).
- Fractions are converted only through from_frac (ia 27-33). It compares Fr(float(q)) exactly with q and widens one ulp, which needs float(q) correctly rounded or at least faithful; CPython's int/int true division is correctly rounded.

Box edges and midpoints (certificate 77-84, 94, 133-137, 146-148, 199, 302; boxes 631-632) are floats shared by neighbouring cells, so the cells tile the domain exactly. The k-cell edges are exact dyadics.
audits.elementary_functions:
exp(-y), ia.py 163-201:
- Range reduction y = n ln2 + r. n is a float seed; r = sub((y,y), mul(n, LN2)) is an interval, checked to lie in [-1e-9, 0.75] or the run raises (185-186).
- Degree-18 Taylor polynomial evaluated by Horner. The bound gamma_{2*18} (Higham's Horner bound) times gamma_18 (coefficient error from the recursive 1/i!, lines 144-146) gives gamma_54 <= 56u(1+1e-12). The truncation term 0.75^19/19! e^0.75 is about 7e-20 < 1e-19 e^0.75, and ez=2.12 >= e^0.75 = 2.1170. Both are applied outward (189-190); I re-derived both.
- Monotonicity in r is used correctly: lower end at r[1], upper end at r[0] (187-188).
- Scaling by 2^-n uses ldexp, which is exact: n <= 1009 keeps the result normal (above 2^-1022).
- y>700 returns [0, 2^-1000], which is valid since e^-700 = 2^-1009.9.
- A tiny negative lower end (>= -1e-300) returns an upper bound of up(1) (196-200).

Phi(t) for 0<=t<2, ia.py 209-236:
- Uses the positive series 1/2 + phi S. The loop stops by n=24 because 4^24/49!! is about 4.8e-18. The relative error of the float sum is at most about 73u, which I re-derived as 3n+N+1 and which is inside the stated 75u and the 1e-13 allowance.
- The geometric tail uses ratio >= t^2/(2n+3), with t2 rounding covered by (1+4u) (230-232).
- The t<1e-100 branch is valid for t>0.

Q(t) for t>=2 is phi(t) times the hull of the depth-n and depth-(n+1) Laplace continued-fraction approximants, each evaluated in interval arithmetic (ia.py 239-256). Classical Stieltjes bracketing for a convergent continued fraction with positive elements makes this a valid enclosure, and the stopping rule never affects validity.

Other functions:
- pi: Machin's formula with an alternating-series remainder (123-133).
- ln 2: sum 1/(j 2^j) with tail < 2/(J 2^J) (150-156).
- Cube roots: verified outward (boxes 194-201, 588-596).
- Roots of P(x)=T: verified with _sgn_f (boxes 81-94). The a priori bound is 5u|r| + u|f| (p, q, two products, one subtraction; 2x exact). The test uses 8u(|r|+T) + 4u|f| + 1e-300. The sign test is sound, and brackets are accepted only when the signs are certified (151, 188); otherwise the run raises (154, 191).

Integration rules:
- E2B: second-order Taylor about the midpoint (certificate 191-215). G'' = g''(m)a^2/36 + g'(m)/6 is increasing for a >= 0 and is bounded by its end values.
- Ib3: monotone Riemann bounds (295-309).
- K_p: midpoint/trapezoid rules on convex f_p (boxes 619-642). I re-derived f''/f >= 57.7 for q >= 0 and >= 120 for q < 0.
- Box Taylor remainder (boxes 351-359): Cauchy-Schwarz cross term on exact Gaussian moments (322-348, 691-703).
- I re-derived the formulas for V_B, V_w, V_BB, V_Bw, V_ww, H_T, V_T, H_B, r_B and x_B in boxes.py 213-267 and NOTE.md 157-178, the H_2 C^1 boundary, the tail polynomials (certificate 240-255), x_b <= |B| + (T/2)^(1/3), and the chi^2 identity and bound (torus 16-21, 154-158). All match the code.

- pi: Machin rational enclosure, then from_frac outward (ia.py 123-137).
- ln2: rational enclosure (150-160).
- sqrt2, sqrt3, sqrt(2 pi) and 1/sqrt(2 pi): computed with isqrt/div (ia 138-140; certificate 42; boxes 25-26).
- 1/12 and 1/72: div enclosures (boxes 687-688).
- 101/100: from_frac (torus 157).

Float literals on the claim path are exact dyadics: 4.5, 1.5, 0.75, -2.25, -0.25, 36k^2 and 3k^2 for k in {1/2, 1, 2}, and S0 products.

Thresholds are used only one-sidedly, as conservative upper bounds or slack: ez=2.12, 1e-19, 1e-12, 1e-13, 2^-1000, 1e-300, 1e-100, 15, 0.006, 1+4e-16.

There are no quadrature nodes or weights on the claim path; Gauss-Legendre appears only in the self-test.

Inputs:

- b is in {0, 1}.
- Variances are exact floats and standard deviations are isqrt enclosures.

Publication (certificate 360-371) uses Decimal(float), which is exact. It subtracts and adds MARGIN*|x| in the default 28-digit context; that context rounds to nearest, but its error of at most about 1e-27 relative is swamped by the 1e-7 margin. Final 10-digit rounding uses quantize with ROUND_FLOOR/ROUND_CEILING. Every published interval therefore contains the raw enclosure.
audits.decisions:
Every claim-path decision uses the correct endpoint, with no tolerance and no fallback that passes on failure.
- Root sign tests: _sgn_f returns ±1 only outside the error bound (boxes 90-94). xbig/xmid accept a bracket only when the lower end equals xm (or |B|/2) or has a certified sign, and the upper end likewise (151, 188).
- H_2 support classification:
  - Bl >= 0 means zero (539).
  - Tl >= upper(|Bl|^3/2) means zero (542).
  - Inside requires Bh<0 and Th < lower(|Bh|^3/2) (546).
  - H2_point uses T >= half[1] for zero and T > half[0] for the ambiguous case, which falls back to the bound H_2(B,T') with T' < T (505-508).
  - _H2_center classifies by the opposite endpoints (516, 526).
- First-order corner choices follow the re-derived monotonicity:
  - V_range (397-398) and H_range (419) are correct.
  - The H_2 corners (550-551, 557) and the big_hessian x and r corners (428-437) are correct.
  - The _cbrt_lo interior minimum (430) lowers XL conservatively.
- Lower clamps at 0 are used only where the integrand is nonnegative: H_range 419 (H = (x+|B|)(2x-|B|)^2 + 2(B_-)^3 >= 0), H2 510/552, EH2t 330, Ik 344.
- Tails enter E[V] with both signs (329) and H/H_2 from above.
- Other guards raise and are never relaxed:
  - eps2 <= 0.006 (torus 154-155);
  - the exp range-reduction check (ia 185-186);
  - the Phi termination cap (ia 226-227);
  - an empty I1∩I2 (boxes 369-373);
  - KMoments alignment (boxes 657-658, ValueError);
  - zero division.
- MAXDEPTH acceptance (certificate 76, 127) and the _mills cap n>4000 (ia 254) return valid but wider enclosures.
- The --check containment (certificate 374-375) uses exact Decimal comparisons. not_looser (378-384) only bounds tightness.
- Slacks of 1e-9, 1e-6 and 1e-12 appear only in the self-test (certificate 623, 631, 651, 662). The self-test can only fail the run and does not affect the published enclosures.
- 'certified': True (463) is written only after certify returns without error.

Python specifics:
- Pure CPython floats (binary64, round-to-nearest; no rounding-mode control).
- No numpy.
- Decimal is used only in publication, as above.
- No assert statements, so -O does not change behaviour.
- Requires math.nextafter (Python 3.9+).
- Even x87 double rounding (error below one ulp) stays covered by the one-ulp widening and by the slack in the a priori bounds.

findings.issue: When a cell edge is exactly 0, div((0,0), s) gives t0 = (-5e-324, 5e-324). _Qiv then calls Q_point(-5e-324), which reaches _Phi_pos_point with a negative t; that function's precondition is t >= 0 and it is not enforced. The t<1e-100 branch returns 0.5 as the lower end of Phi(-5e-324), which is not a valid lower bound (the true value is 0.5 - 2e-324). The enclosure still holds: _Qiv uses only Q_point(t[0])[1] = up(1-0.5) = 0.5+1.1e-16, which exceeds the true Q of 0.5+2e-324. The fix is to clamp t at 0 or route negative t through the symmetric branch.

The upper bound of E[2(B_-)^3] (acc on [0, a1_last] plus the tail on [top, inf)) needs the last cell end fl(fl(top*4000)/4000) to be >= top. The code does not check this. My hand computation for top = fl(12*up(sqrt(2/k))) at k = 1/2, 1, 2 gives an exact round trip, so there is no gap. Any gap would contribute about 1e-40. An explicit check, or using top itself as the last edge, would make this invariant hold by construction.

The 'N_3(0) = 2 sqrt2 check' only tests that two enclosures overlap. That is a consistency check, not a proof of the identity, which is analytic: pi (2pi)^(-1/2) * 4 sqrt2/sqrt(2pi) = 2 sqrt2. NOTE.md line 70 says 'the certificate checks'; this check is not used for any published value.

Shells j > 6 are bounded by 2*term_6 on a hand argument ('consecutive bounds decrease by far more than 1/2'). The true ratio is about e^(-750) times a polynomial factor, and term_6 is already inflated by the 2^-1000 cap, so the bound holds. It is still an a priori claim, not a computed one. The Hermite bound |He_g| <= Hh_g(|y|), the decrease of Hh_a Hh_c e^(-t^2/2) for t^2 > a+c, |d^gG(0)| <= 15 and |1/Theta - 1| <= Theta - 1 all check out.

NOTE.md states r in [0, 0.75] for the exp range reduction. The code accepts r in [-1e-9, 0.75] (ia.py 185), and the polynomial bound (ia.py 163-172) is stated for |z| <= 0.75, so the code is consistent and only the documentation is imprecise.

The self-test compares the enclosures with floating Gauss-Legendre values using relative slack (1e-9, 1e-6 at the H_2 boundary, 1e-12 for the k-moments). This is not a certification decision; it can only cause failure. Soundness of the published enclosures rests on the derivations, which I re-checked, not on the self-test or the mutants.

Platform assumptions that cannot be checked by reading: math.sqrt is correctly rounded (IEEE 754 / C Annex F), and Fraction.__float__ (CPython int/int true division) is correctly rounded, or at least faithful, which from_frac's one-ulp widening needs. Both hold for CPython on standard hardware. There is no explicit NaN guard, but no claim-path operation can produce NaN with these bounded box ranges.

Sound in ia.py.
- add, sub, mul and div (ia.py 36-57) apply one IEEE operation per corner product and then widen with dn/up (math.nextafter, 14-19), lower endpoint down and upper up. One-ulp widening also covers a faithful (not just correct) rounding and the subnormal range.
- div raises when the divisor interval contains 0 (54-55); cdiv raises if the lower bound of |b|^2 is <= 0 (cx.py 55-60).
- isqrt raises on a negative lower endpoint, uses math.sqrt (IEEE correctly rounded) and widens (110-115).
- sqr and pw handle sign cases (72-99). divc and scal take exact float constants (60-69).

findings.issue:
Whether the d = 3 error bound is covered depends on run-time float bits that cannot be checked by reading.
- _sub(a, b, 2) ends at fl(a + fl(b - a)), not at b. When a < b/2, and with a in [2^-6, 2^-5) and b, b - a in [2^-5, 2^-4), writing a = A*2^-58 and b = B*2^-57, the endpoint is b - 2^-57 exactly when B is odd and A = 1 mod 4. In that case the v-sliver (b - 2^-57, b) is left out of the bound on the integral of |f3| dv (line 161).
- v_edges(tb) keeps 0.3/tb and 0.7/tb, and drops 0.5/tb, for 10 < tb <= 15. Both values fall in those binades for about 11.2 < tb <= 12.8.
- _int_v_bound calls v_edges with tb = the upper real abscissa of each t-ellipse slab (149) from _outer_rule('t') (176). For t-panels (8,11) and (11,15), several slab abscissae fall in that window. For example rho = 1.2, T = (11,15), slab j = 2 gives tb ~ 12.4917, which matches NOTE.md's own example (0.024016010673783495, 0.056037358238828154) to about 10 digits, as far as I can compute by hand.
- If the bit condition holds on a reached call, the M at line 176, and with it the Lemma Q term et (194, 209), is not proven. The 1e-12 slack almost certainly absorbs a 2^-57 sliver, but nothing in the code bounds |f3| on that sliver.
- NOTE.md 367-369 says the published run never reaches such a case, citing an external audit of actual calls. That depends on which rho values _search reaches at run time and on the low bits of the slab abscissae, so it cannot be verified without running the code.
- Only d = 3 is affected (T3, c1^(3), I_cand d=3, the d = 3 ratios, and [P] d=3). d = 1 and d = 2 never call _sub. The S/T calls of _sub are exact on the published grids: either Sterbenz applies or a = 0, and b - a lies below b's binade. Their halves only need to cover interior nodes.
- Fix: make _sub return b as its last endpoint, or raise when it does not.

libm pow (float ** int) is trusted in error-bound arithmetic, protected only by relative slack: 1e-12 in error_bound for rho**(-2n) and rho**-2, a factor 2 in the series tails, and 1.5 versus 1.491 plus 1e-12 in the tails, which also assume 15.0**7 and 15.0**9 are exact. Any libm within about 1e3 ulp is safe, but this cannot be verified by reading, and it contradicts NOTE.md 264 ('No libm transcendental is trusted'). Fix: compute these with exact Fractions.

NaN is silently dropped: ia.mul takes min/max over corner products that may include NaN (0*inf), and the running max of bounds discards a NaN (m starts at 0.0). An infinite intermediate would therefore shrink M without any error. By reading I found no route to overflow: exp raises above 700, sin/cos raise above 1e6, magnitudes stay bounded, and wmin*wmin and tmin*tmin cannot underflow on these grids. The packet records this limit (C54-A-FINITE-02, NOTE.md 370-371) but has no finite-result guard.

err_v is a plain float sum() of positive terms; its relative error of about 10u is covered by the (1 + 1e-12) factor. NOTE.md 267 ('Every sum is an interval sum') is not literally true for the error-bound sums.

scal(0.1, X) breaks scal's exact-constant precondition. It is still sound, because 0.1f = (1/10)(1 + 2^-54) and z*2^-54 < ulp(z)/2, so dn(fl(0.1f X_lo)) <= X_lo/10 under correct rounding. This should be documented, or replaced with from_frac(Fr(1, 10)).
Sinc_iv returns (-0.2173, 1.0) for |x| > 3 intervals containing 0, using a stated rather than code-certified constant. It is true: min sin(x)/x = cos(4.4934) = -0.217234 > -0.2173.

enclosure_check returns None, so the check is skipped silently, when coefficients/side24_v1/ENCLOSURE.json is not reachable. This affects only the provenance of the consumed c_(d,24), not the interval arithmetic.

audits.summary:
The verdict is INDETERMINATE, and only the d = 3 results depend on the unresolved point. Apart from that, the code is justified binary64 interval reasoning.
- Every basic operation on the claim path is one IEEE operation followed by one-ulp outward widening, with zero-divisor and negative-sqrt guards.
- pi, ln 2, the Gauss-Legendre nodes and weights, Gamma, Lemma S and all rational constants are exact rationals or outward enclosures.
- exp, log, log1p, atan, sin/cos and the four kernels have correct range reductions and correct, doubled remainder bounds. I re-derived Lemma Q, Lemma A, the complex-box forms and the three tails against NOTE.md.
- Publication and --check use exact outward Decimal containment with no tolerance.

The blocking point is d3._sub (d3.py 40-41): it can drop a 2^-57 sliver at the top of a v-panel. My reading puts the triggering pair (0.3/tb, 0.7/tb) on the published path, through t-slab abscissae near 11.2 to 12.8 in _int_v_bound (d3.py 145-162, 176). Whether a loss actually happens depends on run-time bits, and the packet relies on an external actual-call audit (NOTE.md 367-369) that cannot be checked without running the code.

Two minor points: error bounds trust libm pow with only relative slack, contrary to NOTE.md 264, and Python min/max would silently drop a NaN bound (no route to one found by reading).

Two one-line changes would make this SOUND_AS_INTERVAL_REASONING: have _sub end exactly at b, and compute the error-bound powers in exact Fractions. Alternatively, a reviewed replay could confirm that no reached _sub call loses its endpoint. This record advises the A3 field only; it certifies nothing.

I re-derived the following:

- V_T has sign -B, V_w = -sqrt3 B(4x+B)(2x-B)^(1/2)/x and V_ww = -r(4 - r + r^2).
- g' < 0 and e' = (2-r)^(1/2)(-2 - r - 3.5r^2) < 0.

- H_2 is non-increasing in B and in T on the middle root, which justifies H2_point 505-508.
- The Taylor-moment algebra in taylor_moments3 and the Cauchy-Schwarz remainder in _quad.
- The convexity f''/f >= 57.7 for the k-quadrature, and the exact dyadic k-edges.
- The tail polynomials: x <= |B| + (T/2)^(1/3) gives H <= 17|B|^3 + 8T, and the coefficient sets at certificate.py 244-254 follow.

Every decision either raises an error or only widens. Uncaught ValueError and ZeroDivisionError abort the run. The torus j > 6 shell bound is a correct hand argument with astronomically large slack.

With a in [2^-6, 2^-5) and b, b - a in [2^-5, 2^-4), ties-to-even give b - 2^-57 exactly when B is odd and A = 1 mod 4 (I checked both rounding steps). So 0.3/x1 = (36/1499)(1 + 4.07e-14) = 0.0240160106737835 and 0.7/x1 = 0.0560373582388282, which match NOTE.md 367-368 to within one ulp. Size: the lost sliver can move M only by about 2^-57 sup|f3|. Against the (1+1e-12) slacks (gauss.py 127, d3.py 209), the enclosure would fail only if |f3| on the sliver were about 4000 times the bound on the adjacent sub-interval. Nothing in the code excludes that, but it is not plausible for an analytic integrand.

reviews.reasoning:
I re-read d3.py, gauss.py, cusp.py, cx.py, elem.py, ia.py, consts.py, side24.py (transfer), the certificate.py drivers and publication, and NOTE.md 240-375. I ran no code.

The rest of the path is justified interval reasoning, which supports the audit:
- Gauss-Legendre nodes come from an exact sign change at r +- 2^-150, and the weights use a valid Lipschitz enclosure (|P'_(n-1)| <= n(n-1)/2) (gauss.py 41-112).
- I re-derived the Lemma Q bound from the even-k sum, and the slabs cover the closed ellipse with 1e-12 inflation (gauss.py 124-146).
- cx.py: the complex box forms are valid (the integral hulls of E1, L, A and Sinc, principal Log for Re > 0, the polar cpow).
- cusp.py: the direct-form bounds are valid (|z^a| = |z|^a, _off_cut, H* = conj H(conj w)).
- The safe-form identity holds: 1 - Re Phi = -R E1(R) + e^R (I^2/2) Sinc(I/2)^2.
- Tails: (36/19)^(5/8) = 1.491 < 1.5, |Phi| <= t^-2, the exact s-integral Gamma(21/8)/(8 E^(21/8)), the 0.1874999 < 3/16 clamp, and the s > 3 bound of about 3.5e-289 < 1e-280.
- scal(0.1, X) at d3.py 256 is sound under correct rounding.
- Exact Decimal containment in compare() (certificate.py 430-432).

The _sub calls on S and T are exact. The only non-Sterbenz S pair, (2.8/tb, 0.6), has b - a below b's binade, so its rounding error is less than ulp(b)/2.

The one unresolved dependence is d3._sub at d3.py 40-41, used at 151 and 161. A 2^-57 sliver at the top of a (0.3/tb, 0.7/tb) v-panel can be left uncovered, and the published d = 3 results (T3, c1^(3), the d = 3 ratios and the [P] d = 3 rows) rest on run-time float bits and on an external actual-call audit (NOTE.md 367-369) that cannot be checked by reading.

The gap is real in the reasoning, and the rho = 3.0 calls make it likely to be exercised on the published path. A failure of the final enclosure is not demonstrated, so the verdict is INDETERMINATE, not UNSOUND. d = 1 and d = 2 are unaffected. Two changes would make the record SOUND_AS_INTERVAL_REASONING: make _sub return b as its last endpoint (or raise), and compute the error-bound powers in exact Fractions.
